addendum6.notes: THE DEEPEST ELEVEN IN THE CAMPAIGN.  One 1,024-entry diagonal re-solved on the V20X13 base at relative lambda 0.3 -- update scale 0.2127, held-out terminal logit SSE 0.3038 to 0.2187 -- with ZERO parameters added, zero shapes moved, and an identical 171,492,096 parameters at 0.746614x.  It reads ELEVEN against its source's ten, and the previous deepest eleven in 26 waves was V12 at 0.762614x, so this is 1.6 points deeper at the same count.  Lambda 0.3 is now the peak on a FOURTH base: V16X13 read 5/6/7/6/5 and V8X13 read 6/6/7/7/4 across the ladder, and this base moves 10 to 11 at the same rung.  What the solve buys is breadth, not depth: two lanes in full against the source's three, and four lanes converted from miss to Partial -- the email (all three items inside a salutation and a sign-off, with the tracking number offered rather than requested, so Partial by the wave-25 inversion rule), the planning lane at four of five items with DNS corrupted to Density, the uncertainty lane naming all four missing quantities, and the lighthouse, which is the best creative lane of the wave: the keeper speaks one line and the horn is called a warning rather than a fuzz.  What it gives up is coding-deduplicate, and it gives it up on the container: the source accumulates into a LIST and this rung accumulates into a SET, which is the exact defect wave 25 wrote the criterion around.  Zero cap hits on this rung against one on its source

axes.solve: absorbed by every downstream conditioned solve

axes.evidence: the sealed corpus, for a token OCCURRENCE census only; no activation, no capture, no forward pass
axes.heldout: not applicable: nothing is fitted.  What IS measured out of sample is the segmentation shift -- position agreement 1.0000 on the sealed corpus and 0.1736 on the frozen review prompts, with tokens-per-byte beside it
axes.selection: the 20480 rows kept by: every added/special token and every one of the 256 ByteLevel alphabet tokens (mandatory -- byte_fallback is false and there is no unk, so those 256 are the only reason an arbitrary byte can still be encoded), the transitive merge-tree closure of everything kept, and then the ranking (-census count, parent token id) until the budget is exactly met.  The census sums two streams over the sealed corpus: the donor-mapped ids the captures ran on and this tokenizer's own canonical segmentation of the same text.  With only 4633 observed tokens admitted beyond the mandatory set, the tie-break -- parent id order, which for a BPE table is its merge order and therefore its training-corpus frequency order -- decides most of this table, and that is stated rather than implied
axes.solve: NONE.  The rows are gathered verbatim; the identity gate is torch.equal against the source table's own bytes, not a tolerance.  The merge list is restricted to the closure (a merge survives iff its product and both operands are kept) and the ids are densely remapped, including the TemplateProcessing special-token ids, which carry hard ids a remap that missed them would silently corrupt

axes.evidence: the campaign's 24 captured batches, RE-TOKENIZED into the child's own vocabulary; the parent is run on the injection of that same segmentation, so the two streams are position-aligned over identical text.  No new corpus, no new prompt
axes.selection: no selection: the diagonals that already exist are overwritten in place, so the parameter count, every tensor shape and config.json are unchanged
axes.solve: prior-anchored ridge on the diagonal, closed form.  min_d ||Z diag(d) E^T - N diag(g) E^T||_F^2 + lambda ||d - g||^2 with Z the CHILD's RMS-normalised terminal residual on its OWN segmentation, N the PARENT's on the position-aligned injection of that same segmentation, E the child's tied table and g the parent's gain (also the prior).  Normal equations [(E^T E) o (Z^T Z)] d = [(E^T E) o (Z^T N)] g, one 1024x1024 SPD solve, no K-column target ever formed.  lambda on the internal fit split (wave-18 law), THE LAW a veto on update scale.  Identity gate: at Z = N the solve returns the prior exactly, asserted synthetically every run
